summary: Christine Song, a longtime startup HR leader turned founder of 5to9 Society, explains why she left a decade of being the right hand to venture-backed CEOs to build a vetted, confidential dinner community for founders and operating leaders across Canada. She describes the isolation founders hide behind conviction, the reference checks and Chatham House rules that make her tables safe, and the post-COVID collapse in socializing that makes peer community matter more than ever. The conversation also covers the chip-on-your-shoulder mindset, why executives who don't tell CEOs the truth are a problem, and how AI bots are eroding trust in outreach.
takeaways: Christine says it takes roughly 10 years to build a successful business, so pick something you can enjoy doing for a decade or you will quit in months.
5to9 Society dinners are capped at 12 to 15 people in a private dining room under Chatham House rules, and operators are admitted only after a 15-minute reference call with a CEO they reported to.
Founders rarely get the truth from their own executives because they can fire them; peers at a dinner table have nothing to lose and will tell you what to do.
Christine cites research that the average North American has cut socializing and networking by up to 25% since COVID, which she links to founder loneliness and leaders using AI as a therapist.
The 5 to 9 after work is where the highest performers invest in themselves; do not expect your manager to fund your growth, and reading books or listening to podcasts costs nothing.
A healthy chip on your shoulder means doing something about what pisses you off instead of blaming the world, which is why Christine started her own business after never getting an exit.

David posted on TikTok three times a day for a year and landed a direct line to an American investor by tagging her; Christine landed a billionaire as a surprise dinner guest with a single cold email.
AI-written outreach and comments are destroying trust: when Christine asked an audience how they would feel learning a message or post came from a bot, every hand went down.
